scope: Orbital source records and a preservation lock for every scientific catalog field. The catalog snapshot is first-party evidence, not proof of an upstream attribution. Physical and spin provenance remains in PROVENANCE.md.

units.rotationHours: hours; signed catalog period, with spin-model interpretation in PROVENANCE.md
units.orientationJ2000: pole RA/Dec and prime meridian in degrees; signed spin direction

model: Frozen Kepler ellipses with display compression. Runtime day zero represents J2000; UTC-based date labels are schematic and do not implement a precision TDB/UTC conversion. Moon synchronous periapsis compensation is a display correction, not the source nodal/apsidal propagation. No source validity interval is an accuracy claim for this runtime.

fixed-sun.frame: not applicable to a zero orbit
fixed-sun.elementType: first-party zero-orbit sentinel; neither mean nor osculating
fixed-sun.units: zero AU/km, dimensionless eccentricity, degree angles and day period
fixed-sun.derivation: No orbital solution or derived angles; all zero fields mark a stationary center.
fixed-sun.validity: Scene convention only; does not model solar barycentric motion.

legacy-heliocentric.epoch: J2000 intended by the original catalog comment; upstream epoch unverified
legacy-heliocentric.center: Sun in Helios; original source center unverified
legacy-heliocentric.frame: ecliptic J2000 in Helios; original source plane/equinox unverified
legacy-heliocentric.elementType: unknown; a generic mean-element claim is not verified
legacy-heliocentric.derivation: Original omega/M derivations and rounding were not retained; freeze the existing literals without reconstructing a source by inference.
legacy-heliocentric.validity: Unknown source validity and error bounds. No complete row is attributed to current JPL Table 1.

ceres-horizons.frame: Ecliptic of J2000.0; ICRF reference system
ceres-horizons.units: A in AU, EC dimensionless, IN/OM/W/MA in degrees, PR in days
ceres-horizons.derivation: Direct A, EC, IN, OM, W, MA, PR fields; omega and M are already arguments/anomalies, not longitudes.
ceres-horizons.validity: One retained state at the epoch. Future Horizons solutions may differ; verify solution identity. The frozen runtime ellipse has no ephemeris accuracy interval.

neptune-table-1.timeScale: TDB (JPL calls Teph equivalent to JDTDB)
neptune-table-1.frame: mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000
neptune-table-1.elementType: best-fit Keplerian coefficients; JPL explicitly says these are not mean elements
neptune-table-1.units: a in AU, e dimensionless, I/L/long.peri./long.node. in degrees
neptune-table-1.derivation: omega = (long.peri. - long.node.) mod 360; M = (L - long.peri.) mod 360. No rates used at T=0.
neptune-table-1.validity: The source elements plus rates are fit for 1800 AD - 2050 AD. Helios does not apply rates; its inherited 60189-day period is separately unverified and this source interval is not a runtime accuracy claim.

satellite-de405-le405.table: Planetary Satellite Mean Elements, named satellite row
satellite-de405-le405.frame: ecliptic; table does not separately identify its equinox
satellite-de405-le405.elementType: mean elements of a fitted precessing ellipse, not an instantaneous geometric Horizons snapshot; JPL's epoch caption says osculating mean elements
satellite-de405-le405.units: a in km, e dimensionless, w/M/i/node in degrees, P in days, Laplace pole RA/Dec in ICRF degrees
satellite-de405-le405.derivation: Direct source a/e/w/M/i/node/P columns; w is argument of periapsis. Helios attaches this row directly to its ecliptic J2000 scene.
satellite-de405-le405.validity: JPL does not specify a validity interval on this table and warns against ephemeris computation. P is labeled sidereal period by JPL; Helios uses that literal as its mean-anomaly clock and does not propagate source nodal/apsidal rates.

satellite-mar099.table: Planetary Satellite Mean Elements, named satellite row
satellite-mar099.frame: local Laplace plane; pole RA/Dec in ICRF, node from the reference-plane node on the ICRF equator
satellite-mar099.elementType: mean elements of a fitted precessing ellipse, not an instantaneous geometric Horizons snapshot; JPL's epoch caption says osculating mean elements
satellite-mar099.units: a in km, e dimensionless, w/M/i/node in degrees, P in days, Laplace pole RA/Dec in ICRF degrees
satellite-mar099.derivation: Direct source a/e/w/M/i/node/P columns; w is argument of periapsis, not longitude. Laplace planes are converted once using the printed ICRF pole and the fixed PCK parent pole.
satellite-mar099.validity: JPL does not specify a validity interval on this table and warns against ephemeris computation. P is labeled sidereal period by JPL; Helios uses that literal as its mean-anomaly clock and does not propagate source nodal/apsidal rates.
